title: Histogram and Density Plot Selection
description: Rules for visualizing continuous univariate distributions, bin count optimization, and density curves.
conditions: Displaying univariate continuous feature distribution in report or dashboard
Assessing skewness, modality, and tail behavior visually
recommended_methods: Freedman-Diaconis rule for optimal histogram bin width [bin_width = 2 * IQR * N^(-1/3)]
Rug plot along the x-axis for individual sample density visualization
selection_rules: Always compute bin counts using Freedman-Diaconis rule rather than arbitrary default (e.g. 10 bins)
If sample size N > 1,000, overlay smooth KDE line on top of normalized frequency histogram
Always include clear axis labels with measurement units and median indicator line
limitations: Arbitrary bin widths can obscure or falsely manufacture multimodal peaks
KDE curves can smooth out sharp true cutoffs (e.g. bounded positive features at zero)
source: Freedman and Diaconis (1981) On the Histogram as a Density Estimator
